name: Chimborazo (Minneapolis)
whatItIs: Full-service restaurant serving food of Ecuador and the Andean highlands; owner and chef Marcos Pinguil.
evidence: Own site lists hours and menus, but the Northeaster (June 29, 2026) reported a basement fire in June 2026 and that owners were working to restore the space. No opened page confirms reopening.

name: Chimborazo (St. Paul)
neighborhoodOrCity: Highland area, St. Paul (508 Lexington Pkwy. S.)
whatItIs: Counter-service second location of Chimborazo, opened 2024.
evidence: Own site (2026 copyright) lists current hours: Mon-Thu 11-9, Fri 11-10, Sat 8-10, Sun 8-9, with online ordering.

name: Chimborazo On Wheels
whatItIs: Food truck and event catering from the Chimborazo restaurant family.
evidence: Own site describes the truck but shows no dated schedule.

name: Sabor Cuencano
whatItIs: Ecuadorian breakfast and fast-food restaurant named for Cuenca.
evidence: Own site lists current hours (Mon-Fri 7-3, Sat-Sun 7-8) and online ordering; its manager was interviewed by the Northeaster in July and August 2026.

name: Panadería Ecuatoriana Charito
whatItIs: Ecuadorian bakery, the Northeast franchise of the owner's family bakery; also sells packaged South American foods.
evidence: Northeaster, Aug. 3, 2026, quotes owner Jorge Sanchez and says the bakery has operated about 10 years on Central.

name: La Mesa
neighborhoodOrCity: Bryn Mawr, Minneapolis (230 Cedar Lake Rd. S.)
whatItIs: Neighborhood bistro with Ecuadorian- and Latin-inspired food, owned by Juan Yunga, from Cuenca, and Ann Carlson-Yunga since 2018.
evidence: Own site lists hours (Tue-Sat 5-10 p.m.), reservations and Tuesday Date Night.

name: Los Andes Latin Bistro
neighborhoodOrCity: Uptown (West Lake St.) and Northeast Minneapolis (2300 University Ave. NE)
whatItIs: Family-owned Latin American restaurant named for the Andes; opened a Northeast location in 2026 and hosted EcuaFiesta 2026. Ownership origin not stated in opened sources.
evidence: Own site lists daily hours and Sunday karaoke; Northeaster, May 19, 2026, reports the new Northeast location.

name: Chulla Vida
whatItIs: Ecuadorian restaurant announced with the canopy line "a taste of Ecuador and more."
evidence: Northeaster, March 13, 2025, reported it as coming soon; no opened page confirmed it is operating.

name: El Paraíso
whatItIs: Supermarket and restaurant for Ecuadorian products (chochos, Andean fruits, ají, frozen cuy), with money transfer; co-owned by Columbia Heights firefighter Bertha Orellana.
evidence: Sahan Journal, Nov. 11, 2025 (updated May 4, 2026), reports it opened in summer 2025 and describes current stock. Exact address not given.

name: La Cuencanita Market
whatItIs: Market serving the Ecuadorian community, with money transfer.
evidence: Sahan Journal, Nov. 11, 2025, says it opened recently. Address not given; no later page opened.

name: La Casita Ecuatoriana
whatItIs: Market serving the Ecuadorian community, with money transfer.
evidence: Sahan Journal, Nov. 11, 2025, says it opened recently. Address not given; no later page opened.

name: Killary Crafts
whatItIs: Shop selling traditional Ecuadorian clothing and handmade beadwork designed by owners Juan Cazho and Jeanneth Guaman.
evidence: Pictured in Sahan Journal in March 2024; no 2025 or 2026 evidence found.

name: Mirasol Express
whatItIs: Small Ecuadorian market beside a car repair shop, run by Luis "Alfonso" Quizhpi and family; fresh bread and corn patties.
evidence: Northeaster, June 3, 2021, said it had been open 16 years; no later evidence found.

name: Galápagos Bar and Grill
whatItIs: Restaurant listed as serving traditional Ecuadorian dishes along with other Latin American food.
evidence: Only an undated travel-site listing with reviews was opened.

name: Peace Market
whatItIs: Halal grocery opened 2019 by Moroccan-born owners; stocks foods from the Middle East, Africa, Mexico and Ecuador. Not Ecuadorian-owned.
evidence: Northeaster, June 3, 2021; no later evidence found.

name: Liga Northeast
neighborhoodOrCity: Northeast Minneapolis (Edison High School, Northeast Middle School)
whatItIs: Futsal and soccer league started in 2005 by Jose and Bertha Arias, first for Ecuadorian players, later open to all; over 1,000 players in 2022.
evidence: Northeaster, Feb. 1, 2022; no later evidence found.
